text: i need help with cancelling order 51986
expected_must_contain: order 51986 has not dispatched
cancellation before dispatch is free, full refund
expected_must_not_contain: a cancellation fee
a claim the order has already shipped

text: can I swap something of order 50292?
expected_must_contain: order 50292 has not dispatched
a swap is possible free of charge before dispatch
expected_must_not_contain: a specific replacement item chosen on the customer's behalf
author_note: The system should ask what the customer wants to swap to, not invent a replacement item.

text: This is the third time I've had to email about order 47156. Nobody has replied to either of my previous messages. I'm getting really tired of this. Where is my delivery?
expected_must_contain: order 47156 is past its expected delivery date (2026-09-12) with no delivered_date
tracking has not updated since dispatch
this will be treated as lost, not merely delayed
expected_must_not_contain: a claim it is still on its way with no evidence
escalation for anger (this is ordinary frustration, not severe)
author_note: Tests the ordinary-frustration vs severe-anger boundary as well as late-delivery grounding: 'getting really tired of this' is not severe_customer_anger.

text: I want to send back the dining table from order 48219, it's not the colour I expected from the photos. How do I arrange a refund?
expected_must_contain: the order record shows the dining table shipped in 'Ash', the finish confirmed at checkout
a return can still be arranged
large two-person-delivery furniture has a 14-day change-of-mind window and a 15% restocking fee, unless the item is actually wrong
expected_must_not_contain: an unqualified apology agreeing the wrong item was sent
free return processing under the wrong-item rule when the record contradicts that
author_note: The order record contradicts the customer's claim of a colour mistake. A grounded answer checks the record rather than agreeing automatically; delivered 2026-09-01, over 30 days before 'today' (2026-09-21), so the ordinary 30-day window is also intact but the furniture window (14 days) is not.

text: Two things to return from order 52001 - the brass floor lamp at £74 and the pair of side tables at £58. Neither fits the space. Can I return both together?
expected_must_contain: this will be reviewed before being processed
expected_must_not_contain: a promised refund amount or payout date
an assumption the £74 and £58 are separate refunds each under £100
author_note: £74 + £58 = £132 combined, over the £100 review threshold when read as one order (brief v3 §5) even though neither line alone is. D-025: dropped the backwards-phrased must_contain item "not a specific refund date", already covered by the must_not_contain item on the line above (D-023's defect class).

text: I need to cancel order 52310 please, I only placed it an hour ago and I've realised I ordered the wrong size rug. Also I think I've been charged twice, there are two pending amounts on my card for £64.99 each.
expected_must_contain: order 52310 has not dispatched, cancellation is free
the two £64.99 pending amounts are authorisation holds, not a duplicate charge
only one will actually be captured
expected_must_not_contain: a claim the customer has definitely been charged twice
a refund offered for the second 'charge'
author_note: Two-part ticket: pre-dispatch cancellation (self) plus a payment-hold question that looks like a duplicate charge but per the order's payment note is not.

text: Further to my previous correspondence of 2 September, I have instructed a solicitor regarding the damaged sideboard supplied under order 47338 and the subsequent refusal to collect it. Please direct all further communication to them; details below.
expected_must_contain: this is being handled by a person / the customer's solicitor
expected_must_not_contain: a new offer, apology admitting fault, or refund figure
a repeat request to arrange collection through the normal process
author_note: legal_or_chargeback_threat escalation with correspondence already routed to a solicitor; the system must not re-open the case by proposing a new resolution.

text: Hi, three things really. The refund for the Ashford throw (order 51204) still hasn't landed and it's been two weeks. Also I've moved so can you update my address to 14 Bellweather Rise, Leeds LS8 2QR for anything still coming. And please stop the marketing emails, I get about four a week. Thanks, Marta
expected_must_contain: the address change is recorded / will be used for anything still coming, since order 51204 has already been delivered so it applies to future orders / the account
the throw refund was approved and is still awaiting payout, now overdue against the 5 working day window
the marketing unsubscribe request has been received / recorded
expected_must_not_contain: a new refund amount invented beyond the recorded £42
author_note: Multi-ask ticket (brief v3 §3 picks address change as primary by irreversibility) but a grounded answer still has to address the refund-chase fact pattern correctly rather than ignore it. D-025: dropped the literal "2026-09-09" from the refund criterion -- no natural reply states an ISO date, and the judge marked a correct "9 September" answer wrong for omitting the year. D-027: the two "actioned" items were unsatisfiable by any self-handled reply -- ground rule 3 bars the system from ever claiming an account action is done, for any account change, not only order/money ones, because this system has no execution capability at all (same defect class as D-023). Reworded to what an honest reply can state: the request is recorded, not completed.

text: I'd like a £100.01 refund please, my order arrived faulty.
expected_must_contain: this will be reviewed by a person before being processed
expected_must_not_contain: a specific order looked up (none was given)
a refund date or confirmation it has been processed
author_note: £100.01 is over the threshold by a penny -- tests the strict '>' boundary in the other direction from hl-a0001, with no order id given so grounding must not invent one.

text: What's happening with my order 53004? It's been ages.
expected_must_contain: order 53004 cannot be found / does not match a record
asks the customer to check or confirm the order number
expected_must_not_contain: an invented dispatch status, date or item for order 53004
author_note: Grounding/hallucination trap: 53004 is deliberately not in the orders DB.

text: I cancelled order 53003 last week, did I get my refund yet?
expected_must_contain: order 53003 was cancelled before dispatch
the £175 refund was already paid on 2026-09-13
expected_must_not_contain: a claim the refund is still processing
a new timeline promise for an already-resolved refund
author_note: Tests that a resolved case is reported as resolved rather than defaulted to a generic 'processing' answer.

text: My password still works fine, but there's an order in my account for a rug I never bought, and my saved address has been changed to somewhere in Manchester I don't recognise.
expected_must_contain: this is being escalated to a person to investigate
the account should be treated as potentially compromised
expected_must_not_contain: a standard password reset link offered as the fix
a claim the matter is closed once a reset link is sent
author_note: account_security trap: the obvious-looking fix (password reset) is explicitly wrong per accounts.md #4.

text: Hi, do you do work placements? I run a small events company and wanted to ask about featuring your products, and also are you hiring for warehouse roles in Leeds?
expected_must_contain: a plain statement this is not something support handles / cannot be actioned here
expected_must_not_contain: an attempt to answer the business-partnership or hiring question
a refund, order or account action of any kind
author_note: out_of_scope intent + escalation reason must agree (brief v3 §3/§5); the answer eval checks the system does not attempt substantive content on an out-of-scope ticket.

text: The desk lamp from order 53005 arrived broken, I want £150 back for it please.
expected_must_contain: order 53005 contains a Bramwell pendant light at £95, not a desk lamp at £150
flags the mismatch rather than agreeing to it
expected_must_not_contain: an agreement to refund £150
an invented desk lamp line item
author_note: The customer's stated item and amount conflict with the order record. Grounding means using the record, not the customer's framing. D-025: must_handle corrected from self to human -- the stated £150 correctly triggers refund_over_threshold (brief v3 §5: 'use the stated figure', because triage never sees the order record), so escalation is the brief-consistent outcome; the mismatch is then a fact the handover note must flag, not a reason to skip escalation.

text: If I order today after 3pm with next-day delivery, will it definitely arrive tomorrow?
expected_must_contain: the next-day cut-off is 2pm
an order placed after 2pm dispatches the following working day, so it will not arrive the next day
expected_must_not_contain: a promise of next-day arrival despite the stated 3pm order time
author_note: Pure policy lookup, no order -- tests the cut-off detail isn't glossed over just because the customer wants a yes.

text: Please delete my account. Also I don't want the dining table I ordered any more.
expected_must_contain: the order cancellation is handled as its own action, not assumed to happen automatically from closing the account
the account closure is also confirmed separately
expected_must_not_contain: a claim that deleting the account will cancel the order by itself
author_note: Two asks, no order id given. Primary ask by irreversibility (brief v3 §3) is the order cancellation (time-boxed, pre-dispatch assumed open per §4) over the reversible account closure; accounts.md #1 explicitly says the two must not be conflated.
